label: o as last original token in long (L=8-9) sequences
explanation: Very sparse feature (171 of 6.5M dev steps). Nearly all activation (93% of mass) is on the input token o at the final original position (t=7 or 8, almost always L=9), with a weaker spillover onto the following <DEL> step (7.5% of mass). It never fires in the copy phase, at early positions (t<7), or for L<8. Being o at the last position is close to necessary (mass recall ~0.84) but far from sufficient: only about 1-4% of such steps activate, so precision is very low. The strongest activations come disproportionately from sequences whose first token is y (first_tok=y has 16.7x lift, 58% of mass) or that contain several digits, but adding these conditions loses too much recall to help F1. I could not find a context variable that predicts which of the o-final sequences activate.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 37 cues. Raise it: orig0=y (+2.97), orig2=3 (+2.82), t=8 & in_tok=o (+2.38), orig2=t (+1.69), orig1=3 (+1.50), next_out=y (+1.48). Lower it: next_out=- (-2.58), orig8=- (-2.48), phase=2 (-2.48), n_digits=0 (-1.48).
